title: Cell Biology and Genetics Unit Test
subject: science

items.prompt: Describe two structural features of a mitochondrion that relate to its function in aerobic respiration.

points.text: Names the folded inner membrane (cristae) giving a large surface area
Links the surface area to more sites for respiration enzymes / ATP synthesis

items.prompt: Explain why a red blood cell is described as a specialised cell, referring to two of its features.

points.text: Cites the absence of a nucleus, giving more space for haemoglobin
Cites the biconcave shape increasing surface area for oxygen exchange (or lack of mitochondria so it does not use the oxygen it carries)

items.prompt: A heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) is crossed with a dwarf plant (tt). Determine the expected phenotypic ratio in the offspring, showing your working.

points.text: Sets out the gametes T and t from the heterozygote and t from the dwarf parent
Punnett square or equivalent giving Tt and tt in a 1:1 phenotypic ratio of tall to dwarf

items.prompt: Explain why the phenotypic ratio in a dihybrid cross of two double heterozygotes is 9:3:3:1 only when the two genes assort independently.

points.text: States each heterozygote makes four gamete types in equal proportions only under independent assortment
Links equal gamete proportions through random fertilisation to the 9:3:3:1 ratio

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Structures are named precisely and every claim is tied to a function or mechanism.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Content is relevant but a structure-function or mechanism link is left implicit.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Terms are used loosely and explanations rest on assertion rather than mechanism.
